title: Financial Payments Fraud Decision Workbench
summary: A fraud strategy workbench built from the full 284,807-row MLG-ULB benchmark, with chronological evaluation, calibrated scoring, and a capacity-bounded review queue.
outcome: A fraud operations lead can compare threshold and staffing choices, see captured and missed fraud, inspect anonymized cases, and identify where extra review capacity stops paying back.

deployment.runtime: Python 3.11 container with one scale-to-zero instance and a private read-only Cloud Storage artifact mount

metrics: 68.0% retrospective fraud recall at one review per 1,000 holdout transactions
91.1% retrospective precision in a 56-transaction bounded review queue
0.7744 held-out PR-AUC with a 95% bootstrap interval from 0.6704 to 0.8501
120 reviews required for the post-hoc 80% recall scenario; 2,430 for 90%
57.3% observed fraud-amount recall at the default policy
stages: Validate all source rows and preserve stable lineage
Split train, calibration, and test periods by chronology
Compare baseline and challenger against a predeclared complexity gate
Calibrate the selected model and write one immutable artifact run
Convert threshold and review capacity into a deterministic ranked queue
Serve policy consequences, scenarios, and anonymized drill-downs
architecture: Private full benchmark validated into stable transaction lineage
Chronological train, calibration, and untouched test partitions
Class-weighted logistic baseline and XGBoost challenger
Calibration gate selecting the simpler model before test evaluation
Immutable model, evaluation, and 56,962-row scored holdout artifact run
Dash and Flask decision workbench on bounded Cloud Run
evaluation: Model selection used calibration PR-AUC and a 0.02 minimum challenger lift before any test result was read
Final ranking used one untouched chronological test partition with 75 fraud rows
PR-AUC uncertainty used 300 deterministic bootstrap resamples
Threshold came from calibration; test capacity was capped at one review per 1,000 rows
Recall scenarios rank the same holdout post hoc and are diagnostic, not deployment thresholds
operationalTradeoffs: The challenger scored higher on test but missed the predeclared calibration lift, so the logistic baseline shipped
The default queue captures 68.0% of observed fraud with five non-fraud reviews, while 90% recall needs 2,430 reviews and 2.8% precision
Scale-to-zero and one maximum instance minimize cost but do not provide a production availability objective
The anonymized benchmark supports ranking and capacity analysis but not customer, merchant, channel, fairness, or intervention decisions
disclaimer: The source benchmark is private and anonymized. The public service exposes scored holdout outputs without cardholder, account, merchant, or customer identity. Results are retrospective and do not establish production performance, causal explanation, loss avoided, fairness, or authorization to approve or decline a payment.

presentation.question: How much known fraud can a fixed review team capture, and where does extra capacity stop paying back?
presentation.answer: At one review per 1,000 transactions, 56 reviews capture 51 of 75 observed frauds at 91.1% precision and 68.0% recall. Reaching 80% needs 120 reviews; reaching 90% needs 2,430, exposing the saturation zone.
presentation.decisionSupported: Compare retrospective score thresholds and review staffing levels before proposing an operating policy.
presentation.architectureAlt: Private benchmark data flows through chronological model selection and immutable artifacts into a bounded fraud strategy workbench.
presentation.evaluationMode: Calibration-selected model and threshold, followed by one untouched chronological test evaluation and post-hoc capacity scenarios.
presentation.publicationStatus: Live public portfolio demonstration; not a production payment system.
presentation.licenseNote: Source access and reuse terms were accepted by the owner. The repository does not grant redistribution rights or publish the raw CSV.

securityControls.implementation: Raw source stays local; the hosted container mounts the active run read-only from private Cloud Storage.
securityControls.limitation: Public APIs intentionally expose anonymized scores, outcomes, amounts, elapsed time, and top model signals for the retrospective holdout.

securityControls.implementation: Cloud Run permits one instance, scales to zero, and applies a process-wide token bucket at two requests per second with a 40-request burst.
securityControls.limitation: The in-process bucket resets when the container restarts and is not identity-aware abuse control.

securityControls.implementation: Missing, incomplete, or corrupt artifact runs return an error and HTTP 503 instead of zero metrics.
securityControls.limitation: This validates artifact integrity, not upstream label correctness.

evidence.claim: All 284,807 source rows validate with 492 fraud labels, 31 columns, and no missing values; the raw CSV remains outside Git and Cloud Run.
evidence.method: Full schema validation before chronological partitioning
evidence.caveat: The source contains no operational identity fields.

evidence.claim: The logistic baseline shipped because XGBoost improved calibration PR-AUC by 0.0064, below the predeclared 0.02 complexity gate.
evidence.caveat: The stronger XGBoost test result remained diagnostic and did not reverse selection.

evidence.claim: The selected logistic model reached 0.7744 PR-AUC on the 56,962-row untouched test partition, with a 95% bootstrap interval from 0.6704 to 0.8501.
evidence.method: One chronological holdout and 300 deterministic bootstrap resamples
evidence.caveat: Only 75 fraud rows occur in the test partition.

evidence.claim: At one review per 1,000 transactions, the queue reviews 56 rows, captures 51 of 75 observed frauds, and records 91.1% precision and 68.0% recall.
evidence.method: Calibration-selected threshold plus deterministic held-out capacity ranking
evidence.caveat: Observed labels are retrospective outcomes, not analyst dispositions.

evidence.claim: The smallest score-ranked queue reaching 80% observed recall contains 120 reviews; reaching 90% requires 2,430.
evidence.method: Post-hoc cumulative ranking of the same immutable holdout
evidence.caveat: Scenarios are diagnostic and cannot serve as deployment thresholds without new validation and operating-cost inputs.

evidence.claim: Twenty-two hermetic tests cover data, artifacts, policy, APIs, failure states, request limiting, and release verification.
evidence.method: pytest in local and GitHub Actions environments

evidence.claim: The anonymous Cloud Run service reports ready health and renders the full decision workflow from the active real artifact run.
evidence.method: Anonymous HTTP plus desktop and 390-pixel live-browser acceptance
evidence.caveat: This is a cost-bounded portfolio demonstration, not a production service objective.

evidence.claim: The public service permits one instance, scales to zero, and rejects excess sustained request work with HTTP 429.
evidence.method: Cloud Run configuration inspection and concurrent anonymous HTTP burst
evidence.caveat: The in-process request bucket is neither distributed nor identity-aware.

story.recruiterSummary: A full-data payments-fraud strategy product that turns rare-event model evidence into an explicit staffing decision instead of stopping at a score.
story.technicalNarrative: The pipeline validates every source row, preserves chronology, selects complexity on calibration evidence, evaluates once on an untouched period, and writes one immutable run. The workbench converts that run into threshold and capacity consequences, a deterministic queue, a capacity frontier, and anonymized record evidence.
scalabilityRoadmap: Add authenticated analyst access before using protected operational data
Add durable distributed request controls before permitting multiple instances
Add scheduled retraining and model-freshness monitoring only after a live label source exists
Add customer, merchant, channel, analyst-cost, and intervention outcomes before making operating or fairness claims
story.executiveSummary: At the current review budget, 56 reviews capture 51 of 75 observed frauds with five non-fraud reviews. The next useful step is not simply more model complexity: moving to 80% observed recall needs 120 reviews, while 90% needs 2,430. The product makes that workload curve visible before a strategy owner changes policy.
story.intendedUser: A fraud operations lead comparing score thresholds and review capacity, supported by an analyst inspecting the bounded queue.

example.title: Deciding whether to fund an extended review tier
steps: Read the current operating point: 56 reviews, 68.0% recall, 91.1% precision
Select the 80% retrospective scenario and see the queue rise to 120 reviews at 50.0% precision
Compare the 85% and 90% points to locate the saturation zone
Inspect captured and non-fraud queue records with anonymized model signals
Take the measured workload trade-off into staffing and policy review without treating it as a production threshold

technologyDecisions.technology: Class-weighted logistic regression with Platt calibration
technologyDecisions.rationale: The challenger missed the predeclared calibration lift needed to justify extra complexity, while the baseline produced calibrated probabilities for threshold analysis.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Promote XGBoost because its held-out test PR-AUC was higher
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The simpler model gives up diagnostic test lift to preserve a selection rule fixed before test evaluation.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Model, evaluation, partition report, and scored holdout remain tied to one validated run ID, so every dashboard number resolves to the same evidence.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Recompute policies from multiple stores or retrain during serving
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Training stays owner-operated and freshness is manual until a real label source and cadence exist.

technologyDecisions.technology: Dash and Flask in one process
technologyDecisions.rationale: One read-only process serves policy controls, APIs, charts, queue filtering, and drill-down without introducing infrastructure unsupported by the data.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Kafka, Spark, Redis, SQL, CDC, and separate API and frontend services
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The compact topology does not simulate streaming or multi-service production behavior.

technologyDecisions.technology: Scale-to-zero Cloud Run with private Cloud Storage artifacts
technologyDecisions.rationale: The complete real artifact run can remain private while the decision surface stays publicly reachable at bounded cost.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Always-on compute, a public artifact bucket, or a generated substitute dataset
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Cold starts remain possible, and the one-process request limiter cannot support a multi-instance production service.

evidence.label: Fraud recall at one review per 1,000
evidence.context: 51 of 75 observed frauds captured in a 56-row queue
evidence.method: Calibration-selected threshold and deterministic chronological holdout ranking
evidence.meaning: The default queue captures over two-thirds of observed fraud while reviewing 0.098% of holdout rows.

evidence.label: Retrospective queue precision
evidence.context: Five of 56 reviewed rows are observed non-fraud
evidence.method: Observed outcomes inside the same bounded queue
evidence.meaning: Most default-policy review work is useful within this retrospective benchmark.

evidence.label: Held-out PR-AUC
evidence.context: 95% bootstrap interval from 0.6704 to 0.8501 on 56,962 test rows
evidence.method: Untouched chronological test period and 300 deterministic bootstrap resamples
evidence.meaning: The selected model ranks rare fraud outcomes materially above the holdout base rate, with uncertainty made explicit.

evidence.label: Minimum reviews for 80% observed recall
evidence.context: 64 more reviews than the default queue for nine additional fraud captures
evidence.method: Post-hoc cumulative ranking of the immutable holdout
evidence.meaning: An extended tier remains compact at 80%, but the workload curve degrades sharply beyond it.

limitations: The benchmark is static, anonymized, and spans roughly two elapsed days without calendar timestamps.
Only 57 fraud rows occur in calibration and 75 in test, so sampling uncertainty is material.
No card, customer, merchant, channel, geography, analyst disposition, intervention outcome, or live feedback exists.
Source amount is not realized fraud loss or loss avoided.
The public service is a bounded demonstration and does not establish production availability, latency, throughput, or security.

bulletCandidates.bullet: Selected a calibrated logistic fraud model over XGBoost after the challenger missed a predeclared 0.02 calibration PR-AUC lift gate, then measured 0.7744 PR-AUC on an untouched chronological holdout.

Converted 284,807 payment records into a capacity-bounded review policy that captured 51 of 75 observed frauds at 91.1% precision, and quantified the queue expansion from 120 reviews at 80% recall to 2,430 at 90%.

Built a replayable model-artifact contract and deployed the complete scored holdout through a scale-to-zero Cloud Run service with private read-only storage, one maximum instance, and bounded anonymous request work.
